description: Covers expert picks review, checked 7 Nov 2026: free picks, who owns Covers, which records you can check, the free contests, and what users say.
dek: Covers is a long running betting media site that gives away expert and computer picks for free and runs free contests with cash prizes. It sells no picks package that we could find. It earns from sportsbook and prediction market offers placed beside the picks, and it shows no full graded record for its own experts.

short_answer: Covers is a real, established business. Its About page names the operator, CS Media Ltd, and says Covers is part of Genius Sports, a company listed on the New York Stock Exchange. The picks are free to read, so the legitimacy question is not about a refund or a package.

The open question is whether the picks win. The picks pages show who made each pick and roughly when, but we found no graded log of wins, losses and units for any analyst or for the computer picks. The few performance figures we found, such as a 19.79% ROI in one analyst's bio, are the site's own claims with no log behind them.

Covers also runs free contests, King of Covers and Streak Survivor, where users' picks lock at game time and are graded by Covers in units. Those leaderboards are the most checkable records on the site, but they belong to users, not to the Covers experts, and Covers runs them itself.
pricing_intro: Covers sold nothing for its picks on 7 Nov 2026. The About page says its core products are offered "free of charge, with no signup or subscription." Below is what we saw and what it costs.
pricing: Expert picks and best bets (all leagues)
Free to enter. Season top prizes shown from a $100 Amazon gift card (CFL) to $3,000 cash (NFL)
Contest units are not real money
Free. $100,000 cash for a 25 pick win streak
No deadline, per the contests page
guarantee: There is no guarantee because there is no price. Covers does not charge for its picks, so a losing pick costs the reader only what they bet on it. Betting losses are never covered by anyone.

The contests have written rules. They say no purchase is necessary, that contest units are not real money, and that cash prizes are paid only to a valid PayPal account, up to 4 to 6 weeks after the winner provides the needed details. The rules also say contests are void in United States territories, the Province of Quebec and where prohibited by law, and that Canadian winners must answer a skill question.

claims_note: The ROI and unit claims sit in writer bios, not next to a record. The bio does not say how many bets the 19.79% covers, what prices were taken or where the bets were logged. An ROI on one season of best bets can swing widely, and a reader cannot check it from the page.

The star ratings come from Covers' own projections compared with the odds. A positive expected value rating is a forecast, not a result, and we found no page that grades how 5 star picks have done over time.
record: What a reader can verify: the King of Covers contests. The rules say picks can be made only until a game starts, cannot be changed once submitted, and are graded at standard prices (risk 110 to win 100 on sides and totals, the moneyline in MLB and NHL). The Money Leaders board on 7 Nov 2026 showed full won, lost and pushed counts for each user, for example a leader at +63679 units on 1703-1544-25, 52.43% winners. Covers runs and grades these contests itself, so they are not third party results, and they cover users, not the Covers analysts.

What is the seller's own marketing: the expert and computer picks. Each pick on the NFL page shows the analyst and a rough time such as "Pick made: yesterday," but we found no graded log, no season record and no units total for any analyst or for the computer picks. The only performance numbers we found were short claims in writer bios.

History: a Gambling911 article dated 20 Jul 2022 reported that the Covers expert picks section, which it said had run for nearly 25 years, was being closed, with a handful of its handicappers moving to WagerTalk. We did not find a paid Covers picks product on 7 Nov 2026.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Covers analyst or Covers computer pick is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Covers picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: on the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even, so free picks still need a full record before they mean much.

customers_intro: Customer evidence on Covers is mostly about the site and its free contests, not about whether the expert picks win. Below is what we read and how much weight it carries.

customers.text: Trustpilot showed a TrustScore of 4.7 from 264 reviews, with 88% five star and 3% one star. The most recent reviews, from 11 Sep to 26 Oct 2026, mostly praise the free contests and prompt prize payouts; one five star review still said payouts were getting complicated. Trustpilot said Covers has not invited customers recently and that the profile is claimed.

Among the one star Trustpilot reviews, three complain that the picks lose, for example that expert picks never hit and that three MLB picks all lost. Others complain about a contest disqualification for multiple entries, a missed NFL Survivor deadline and a 2024 site redesign. One more recent one star review is about a different company, XCover, filed under Covers.

The Covers iPhone app, sold by CS Media LTD and free to download, showed 4.7 stars from 470 ratings. The visible reviews praise the layout and the expert picks; one notes that links in columns go straight to FanDuel and DraftKings. App ratings judge the app, not pick results.
The Covers testimonials page quotes members praising the forums, the matchup data and the free contests, including one who says he won $1,000. These are chosen and published by Covers.
We found no Reddit thread that evaluates the Covers expert picks record, and no BBB profile we could confirm for covers.com.

conflicts: Covers earns from the betting operators it promotes. Its menus carry sportsbook, casino, sweepstakes casino and prediction market promo code pages. Its DraftKings promo page says the offer applies when you sign up "through our exclusive link" and that affiliate link relationships are disclosed. The same page says its experts do not accept compensation for a specific rating.

The picks sit beside those offers. On 7 Nov 2026 the NFL picks page showed us a Kalshi "Exclusive $60 Bonus" with code MAX60 and a "Featured Trade" banner, and the odds next to each pick came from prediction markets and betting apps. What appears may depend on where you are. We saw no disclosure next to the picks themselves.
Covers is part of Genius Sports, a sports data company listed on the New York Stock Exchange, according to the About page.
strengths: Free. There is no package to buy and nothing to refund.
A named operator and parent company, and named analysts with bios.
Each pick shows the analyst, the market and the odds, and contest picks lock at game time with full won and lost counts.
concerns: No graded record for any Covers analyst or for the computer picks.
The only performance figures are short claims in writer bios, such as a 19.79% ROI.
Promo codes and prediction market offers sit beside the picks, and Covers earns from them.
Contest leaderboards are run and graded by Covers itself and cover users, not its experts.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: Covers is a real, long running media business operated by CS Media Ltd and part of Genius Sports, and its picks are posted with the analyst's name before games. We could not verify that the picks win over time, because Covers shows no graded record for its analysts.
How much do Covers expert picks cost?
Nothing. On 7 Nov 2026 the picks, computer picks, contests and iPhone app were all free, and we found no paid picks tier. Covers earns from sportsbook and prediction market offers instead.
Do Covers experts have a verified record?

No. We found no graded log for any Covers analyst or for the computer picks, only claims in bios such as a 19.79% ROI. The King of Covers boards show full graded records, but for users, and Covers grades them itself.
Are Covers expert picks worth it?

They cost nothing, so you get written analysis, odds and the reasoning behind each pick for free. What is unproven is whether following the picks makes money, so a record you keep yourself is the only way to judge them.
